headline: South Asia: Loose talk
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Loose talk.
- Africa: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
- Persian Gulf Region: US base in Bahrain remains low-staffed months after Iranian drone, missile strikes - report.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: RELIEF LAWSUIT - Pastor challenges NIDS requirement for hurricane aid.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 22 hours ago: RELIEF LAWSUIT - Pastor challenges NIDS requirement for hurricane aid.
Pastor Jeffrey Shuttleworth has filed a judicial review application in the Supreme Court challenging the Government’s decision requiring Jamaicans to register under the National Identification System (NIDS) to access Hurricane Melissa relief assistance. The senior pastor of Freedom Come Ministries International wants the Supreme Court to declare the decision illegal, null and void, and quash the requirement through an order of certiorari, as well as award costs.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 22 hours ago: Constitutional red flag raised over power to sell property for unpaid fees.
Solicitor General Marlene Aldred on Thursday raised a red flag in relation to Section 35(1) of the Registration (Shared Community) Act 2026, arguing that it is not consistent with Section 15 of the Constitution. Her pronouncement followed committee member Cleveland Tomlinson’s identification of an inconsistency in the bill, which he said warranted careful review.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Dismantling of policies against violence leaves women with fewer tools to escape.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 11 hours ago: Dismantling of policies against violence leaves women with fewer tools to escape.
Organizations warned that, since 2024, there are less measures to allow victims to find a way out of abusive contexts La entrada Dismantling of policies against violence leaves women with fewer tools to escape se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 9 hours ago: US ICE releases Argentine acrobats after 20 days of arrest.
Agustín Baccega and Gustavo Romanello, a couple from Córdoba, were released on bail. One was seen with an ankle monitor La entrada US ICE releases Argentine acrobats after 20 days of arrest se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.
- The Moscow Times, 17 hours ago: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.
In St. Petersburg, falling drone debris reportedly wounded a 44-year-old woman after damaging an apartment building.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 16 hours ago: "They were trying to build their lives": IT couple killed in Russian drone attack on Kharkiv.
A Russian Shahed drone hit a 15th-floor flat in Kharkiv on 26 November, killing 38-year-old IT specialists Daria and Valerii along with their cat.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: Russians attack civilian business in Zhytomyr Oblast: one killed, 12 injured.
One person was killed and 12 were injured in a Russian strike on a civilian business in Zhytomyr Oblast's Malyn hromada on the afternoon of 27 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 15 hours ago: Russian forces attack Lozova with jet-powered drones, injuring two people.
Russian forces struck Lozova in Kharkiv Oblast with jet-powered drones on 27 November, injuring two people and sparking fires at a house and warehouse.
Southern Europe - bottom line: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
- Politico Europe, 14 hours ago: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
Poland's defense minister said it would be “wrong” not to use the software, despite concerns over reliance on American technology.
- Politico Europe, 19 hours ago: ‘Islam is Sharia’: Germany’s far-right leader attacks Le Pen on Muslims and Europe.
AfD’s Alice Weidel talks mass deportations, the right to Israel’s existence and peace with Russia.
- Balkan Insight, 21 hours ago: Democracy Digest: V4 Remain Critical of Budget as EU Summit Ends Without Deal.
Elsewhere, Ukrainian youth in hospital after setting himself on fire opposite Warsaw’s presidential palace; postal voting scrapped for Slovakia’s 2027 election; EU Parliament warns against Czechia’s public media reforms.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
- Africanews, 19 hours ago: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
Algeria on Thursday condemned what it called the ‘spillover’ of the war in Ukraine into Libya, after Kyiv’s attack on two Russian vessels off eastern Libya. Two Libyan soldiers were killed in Sunday’s drone strikes which sank a Russian warship and targeted a cargo ship in Libyan waters.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Italy says not informed about Ukraine drone strike on Russian ships in Libya.
Italy has joined the voices expressing concern about Ukraine’s attack on Russia ships in Libyan waters. Rome was not informed of Sunday’s drone strike, the country’s foreign minister told parliament on Thursday, warning that further military action could jeopardise efforts to reunify Libya.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one day ago: Sudan: UN Condemns Drone Strikes That Killed 17 Civilians in Blue Nile.
[Dabanga] The United Nations has condemned drone strikes in Blue Nile that reportedly killed 17 civilians in Ed Damazin, as fighting escalates, and displacement deepens across the region. UN Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday that the UN remained "deeply concerned by the escalation of hostilities in Blue Nile state", which had reportedly caused civilian deaths and injuries.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 16 hours ago: Nigeria: 3 Killed in Attack On Hausa Quarters in Delta.
[Daily Trust] Three persons have been killed following an attack by suspected hoodlums on the Hausa quarters in Warri, Warri South Local Government Area of Delta State.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: US base in Bahrain remains low-staffed months after Iranian drone, missile strikes - report.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: US base in Bahrain remains low-staffed months after Iranian drone, missile strikes - report.
Despite negotiations between Washington and Tehran, Iranian attacks on Bahrain have not stopped, with the most recent attack targeting an undisclosed US military base in the country.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Iran war live: Italy says drone in deadly Kuwait attack was made in Iran.
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says the drone behind the deadly Kuwait strike was made in Iran.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Israeli strike on Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza kills two staff.
MSF says Israeli attack on Gaza clinic a 'direct hit' and calls for those responsible to be held accountable.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: IDF thwarts weapons smuggling attempt along eastern border, seizes six pistols.
The incident follows separate police investigations earlier this month into illegal weapons possession in the West Bank, including an operation in which four protected gazelles were discovered.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Malawian Killed Fighting for Russia in Ukraine War.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 22 hours ago: Malawi: Malawian Killed Fighting for Russia in Ukraine War.
[Nyasa Times] The family of a Malawian driver who vanished from Blantyre has been left reeling after learning he was killed while fighting for Russia against Ukraine.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 18 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Police to Name and Shame Companies Selling Counterfeit Agricultural Inputs.
[New Zimbabwe] THE Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) has warned that it will name and shame backyard garages, unregistered companies and individuals involved in manufacturing and selling counterfeit agricultural inputs to farmers.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 23 hours ago: South Africa: South Africa's Border Management Plans Drone Surveillance and Tighter Security for 2026/27 Festive Season.
[New Zimbabwe] The South African Border Management Authority (BMA) is preparing to intensify border security during the 2026/2027 festive season, including deploying drones at vulnerable crossing points to curb illegal activity.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Loose talk.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Loose talk.
WHERE the Iran war goes, Donald Trump is known for his fantastical pronouncements. Trapped in a conflict of his own making, which he cannot find an honourable exit from, perhaps the US president expresses his frustration through these questionable remarks. Speaking to his troops recently, Mr Trump said hypothetical Iranian atomic weapons could cause a “nuclear holocaust”, which is why Tehran’s nuclear ambitions needed to be curbed. He also termed the Iranian leadership “crazy”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement’s top decision-making body on Friday reviewed the regional security situation and condemned “persistent and heinous” Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. A meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) was held in the federal capital, where authorities announced a public holiday and imposed special movement restrictions in view of the high-level gathering. A local holiday was also announced in Rawalpindi. The SPDC comprises the foreign and defence ministers and top military officials of the three countries.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Pakistan Shaheens cruise into Asia Cup Rising Stars final with five-wicket win over Bangladesh ‘A’.
Pakistan Shaheens produced a composed five-wicket victory over Bangladesh ‘A’ in the second semi-final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars on Friday, chasing down a target of 233 with 28 balls to spare to book their place in Sunday’s final against Sri Lanka ‘A’. The defending champions reached 233-5 in 45.2 overs after Bangladesh ‘A’ had posted 232-8 in their 50 overs. Hasan Nawaz, who made 62 and claimed two wickets, was named player of the match.
- The Hindu - International, 10 hours ago: Saudi strike kills 11 in Yemen, reports Houthi media.
The latest incidents came a day after a deadly Houthi attack on a Saudi oil refinery, and add to a growing tally of violence since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer

- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Taiwan is expanding its military draft. Will those troops make a difference?.
Taiwan’s move to toughen up on exemptions to military service has sparked anxiety among some young men facing conscription and raised questions over whether expanding recruitment will actually strengthen the island’s combat readiness. While the government argues that limiting exemptions will make conscription fairer and ease personnel shortages, critics warn that recruiting men previously deemed medically unsuitable could endanger their health, complicate training and undermine morale. Chinese-made long-range radar equipment has been spotted at Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base during the ongoing Golden Dragon 2026 exercises, a move likely to draw fresh attention to the air surveillance capabilities at the Chinese-funded naval facility. Photos and video released to local media showed an LCQ-776 air surveillance and early warning radar alongside Cambodian troops and mounted on a truck with a Royal Cambodian Armed Forces licence plate. For five years, one name card has been missing from the grand circular table at the Association of Southeast Asean Nations biannual leaders’ summit: Min Aung Hlaing. As president of Myanmar, he should by diplomatic convention sit alongside the 10 other leaders of the Southeast Asian bloc at its regular get-togethers. China has for the first time sent its main battle tanks via an amphibious transport dock to Southeast Asia for a 15-day joint military exercise with Cambodia. The drills began on Wednesday at the Cambodia-China Joint Support and Training Centre, which opened early last year at Ream Port – a strategically located Cambodian naval base. A North Korean defector moving north toward the inter-Korean border fence in Cheorwon County was apprehended by South Korean troops Thursday evening, according to Seoul’s defense authorities. India - bottom line: Defence Chief Warns Of Security Risks From China-Pak-Turkey Military Ties.
- NDTV - Top Stories, just now: Defence Chief Warns Of Security Risks From China-Pak-Turkey Military Ties.
Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General NS Raja Subramani said that Pakistan could gain access to advanced Chinese capabilities in intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), as well as positioning, navigation and timing systems.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Why does your Wi-Fi work even when radio signals bounce off walls?.
The evolution of Wi-Fi technology is a fascinating tale of global collaboration. It began with Hedy Lamarr and George Antheil's innovative frequency-hopping idea during World War II. Subsequent advancements were made by CSIRO researchers in Australia, who enhanced indoor wireless communication. The U.S. played a crucial role by opening up radio frequencies for unlicensed use, setting standards that paved the way for the wireless networks we rely on today.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Alleged machete attack on NT woman by partner prompts police search.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Alleged machete attack on NT woman by partner prompts police search.
Police are searching for a man who allegedly attacked his 22-year-old female partner with a machete, resulting in her receiving "serious injuries" to her left arm.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Ukrainian psychiatrists training in Australia to treat trauma at home.
Mental health practitioners from the front line of Ukraine's war head home with Australian stories to share.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Calls for AI road signs after increased cassowary road deaths.
Cassowary advocates in Far North Queensland are questioning why a successful AI road sign trial hasn't been rolled out, as road deaths of the endangered bird almost double this year.
- ABC News Australia, 5 hours ago: Unoccupied house collapses in Mornington Peninsula landslide.
People are being warned to stay away from the landslide as authorities assess its impact, which includes damage to a house.
